definitions.explanation: Having an excessively high opinion of oneself and looking down on others. Describes both the attitude and the person who displays it.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{高慢|こうまん}な{人|ひと}だ。
{高慢|こうまん}な{態度|たいど}を{取|と}ると、{嫌|きら}われる。
examples.english: If you act arrogantly, people will dislike you.

examples.japanese: {成功|せいこう}してから{彼女|かのじょ}は{高慢|こうまん}になり、{昔|むかし}の{友人|ゆうじん}を{見下|みくだ}すようになった。
examples.english: After her success, she became arrogant and started looking down on her old friends.

notes:
Describes a deeply negative trait of excessive pride and contempt for others. Written with the kanji for 'high' ({高|たか}) and 'arrogance' ({慢|まん}), emphasizing both elevated self-regard and dismissive attitude toward others.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {高慢|こうまん}な{態度|たいど} — arrogant attitude
- {高慢|こうまん}な{人|ひと} — arrogant person
- {高慢|こうまん}ちき — conceited, stuck-up (colloquial, slightly old-fashioned)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {傲慢|ごうまん} — arrogant, overbearing; very close synonym, slightly stronger and more literary
- {偉|えら}そう — acting important; more colloquial and less severe
- {横柄|おうへい} — domineering, overbearing; focuses on rude behavior toward others
- {尊大|そんだい} — haughty, self-important; more formal/literary

USAGE:
The compound {高慢|こうまん}ちき (also written {高慢|こうまん}ちきな) is a colloquial intensified form meaning 'stuck-up' or 'full of oneself.'
